internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 15 occurrences the root marks a two-sided, terms-bearing, sealed exchange. As a bare noun (bayʿ) it names the finalized exchange-event itself: the commercial transaction that ceases on the Last Day (2:254, 14:31), that is licit as against ribā (2:275 twice), that must not distract from or displace remembrance and prayer (24:37, 62:9), and — decisively for the unity claim — the exchange with God in which believers hand over selves and wealth against the Garden (9:111 bi-bayʿikum, explicitly glossed by the verse itself with ishtarā, 'purchased'). Form III (bāyaʿa, 6x: 48:10 twice, 48:18, 60:12 twice, 9:111) is the same exchange directed at a personal counterpart: the pledge scenes, where the hand-imagery is explicit ('the hand of God is above their hands', 48:10) and the terms are itemized ('pledge you ON the condition that they not associate...', 60:12) — allegiance and obedience handed over against acceptance, forgiveness, and reward. Form VI (tabāyaʿtum, 2:282) is the mutual enactment among ordinary parties, embedded in a passage about debts, terms, and witnessing — again exchange-with-ratification (witnesses seal it). The one resistant item is 22:40 (biyaʿ, plural), which denotes a class of worship-buildings; there the root contribution survives only as naming motivation: houses in which the God-ward exchange-compact (the sense fixed internally by 9:111 and 48:10) is enacted and God's name remembered — coherent, but not demonstrably a live synchronic semantics of the word.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue: reciprocal terms-bound hand-over sealed between two parties. FORM: bare noun = the exchange-event/transaction as a thing (bayʿ; plural biyaʿ in 22:40 lexicalized to venues); Form III adds directedness at a specific personal counterpart (always with an addressee suffix or divine object: yubāyiʿūnaka / yubāyiʿūna llāha / bāyiʿhunna) — this, not the root, supplies the 'allegiance-pledge' flavor; Form VI adds symmetric mutuality among plural parties (2:282 tabāyaʿtum). CONSTRUCTION: bāyaʿa ʿalā + terms (60:12) makes the conditions explicit; bi- in 9:111 (bāyaʿtum bihi) marks the instrument/content of the compact. CONTEXT supplies the counter-values (goods vs. price; selves vs. Paradise; obedience vs. acceptance) and the eschatological negation ('a day with no bayʿ') — none of these belong to the root itself.

internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 22:40 — biyaʿ appears in a list of demolishable buildings (ṣawāmiʿ, biyaʿ, ṣalawāt, masājid) 'in which God's name is much remembered'. The word denotes a building-type, not an exchange-event; no transaction, parties, or terms are on the surface of the verse. The reconciliation (venues of the covenant-exchange with God) is internally motivated but inferential.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That byE means narrowly 'commercial selling', with the pledge uses (48:10, 48:18, 60:12) being a separate 'allegiance' sense. This fails internally: 9:111 fuses both in one verse — the believers' bayʿ (noun) is the very thing they bāyaʿtum with God, and the verse frames it with ishtarā (God 'purchased' selves and wealth for the Garden). The commercial and pledge uses are one construct: exchange of counter-values under terms. Conversely, a maximally broad 'commitment/covenant' reading over-generates and collapses into ʿ-h-d.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Vs. ʿ-h-d (covenant): ʿahd can be unilateral obligation or promise; byE requires bilateral hand-over of counter-values (9:111 uses both in one verse — the ʿahd is God's side, the bayʿ is the two-sided transaction). Vs. sh-r-y (buy/sell): sh-r-y in the packet's own context (9:111 ishtarā) profiles one party's acquisition/disposal; byE profiles the sealed two-party exchange as such. Vs. t-j-r (tijāra): tijāra is ongoing profit-seeking activity, byE the discrete concluded transaction — 24:37 and 2:282 place them side by side as non-synonyms. The residue is falsifiable: it predicts byE never marks a one-sided gift, promise, or unratified intention — no occurrence contradicts this.

occurrence_dispositions.note: biyaʿ (pl. of bīʿah) is a concrete architectural count-noun denoting non-Muslim houses of worship, coordinated in a four-member enumeration of building types (ṣawāmiʿ/biyaʿ/ṣalawāt/masājid) whose governing predicate is 'would have been demolished' — a purely architectural frame. Separating the layers: (form) it is neither the exchange-event noun bayʿ nor the Form III pledge bāyaʿa nor the Form VI tabāyaʿtum; (derivation) bīʿah is a distinct lexeme, widely regarded as a Syriac/Aramaic loan, joined to b-y-ʿ only by folk/naming motivation; (participants) the reciprocal-exchange schema is wholly uninstantiated — no two counter-parties, no counter-values, no ratifying/sealing act; the referent is a passive physical structure. The frozen 'ratified reciprocal hand-over / binding finalized exchange-compact' contribution therefore does not hold as a live synchronic sense here; it can be reinstated only by importing the God-ward exchange of 9:111/48:10 as the reason such houses exist. This is not a Basmala token-position artifact (22:40 is not Basmala), so STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY does not apply. The occurrence genuinely resists the unified contribution and is not forced to CONSISTENT — consistent with the shard's own concession that the sense survives only as naming motivation, 'not demonstrably a live synchronic semantics of the word.'
